_comment: FROZEN SNAPSHOT — feature 013, T014. Every consent revision that has ever been
published, field-for-field. registry-guards.test.ts compares CONSENT_REGISTRY
against this file, so editing or removing a published entry fails CI. History is
the point (FR-043b), so history is enforced, not trusted.
APPEND ONLY. A published entry in this file is never edited and never removed. A
new revision is added HERE and to lib/consent/registry.ts in the SAME PR as the
wording it describes (research.md §6.1). If a guard fails because this file and the
registry disagree, the registry is what changed illegitimately — fix the registry,
do not 're-baseline' the snapshot.
terms_privacy@2026-07-26.1 is the first entry this snapshot has ever locked (P3,
T023). camera_inference@2026-07-26.1 was locked next (P4, T040), alongside the camera
wording in lib/consent/copy.ts. From here neither can ever be edited.
2026-08-12 (#198): both texts gained a second revision in one PR — the terminology
change that makes "check-in" mean the camera-based monitoring session in the
documents as well as the app, and renames the text questionnaire to the weekly
work-environment survey. Both classified material; both now locked here too.
2026-08-15 (feature 014): terms_privacy gained a third revision — the Privacy
Policy's new suggestion-records data class and its ninety-day retention statement.
Classified material (Mohamed's decision, docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-15);
camera_inference untouched. Locked here in the same PR as the wording.

terms_privacy.rationale: Initial publication of the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy. The first revision of a text is material by definition — there is no earlier wording anyone could already hold, so every user must be asked. Published together with the documents themselves in lib/legal/copy.ts (feature 013, P3).

Terminology (#198). The documents previously reserved "check-in" for the text questionnaire and called the camera capture a "monitoring session", while the application's primary action read "Start check-in" and turned a camera on. Both documents now say plainly that a check-in IS the camera-based monitoring session, and the questionnaire is renamed throughout to the weekly work-environment survey. Judged MATERIAL, not cosmetic. Nothing about what is collected, where it goes, who can see it, or how long it is kept has changed — but the words that tell a reader which of two things a consent covers have, and one of those two things turns on a camera. A person who accepted the earlier wording accepted a document in which "check-in" meant the text questionnaire; under this revision the same word means the webcam capture. Asking again is the only honest reading of that, and it is what FR-043a's "judgement made by a person" is for — a text-diff heuristic would plausibly have called a noun swap cosmetic. Re-prompting every existing holder was accepted as the cost of the change when it was decided. Published together with the wording itself in lib/legal/copy.ts.

Feature 014 (recommendations). The Privacy Policy gains a wholly new recorded data class — suggestion records: what was suggested, what was opened, whether it helped, and what was swapped away — plus a ninety-day retention statement for that class in the same policy-not-a-mechanism framing as monitoring readings. Judged MATERIAL. The published criterion is that a material revision changes what you are agreeing to, and an acceptance recorded before this revision covered a policy that did not disclose this recording at all; a new class of recorded behavioural data sits above the bar #198 set with a terminology re-mapping. The counter-reading — additive disclosure of owner-private records derived from readings already consented to, closer in consequence to the 2026-08-13 band rename that was judged non-material — was considered and rejected: the band rename reworded an existing value inside an already-disclosed category, while this revision discloses recording that no accepted text mentioned, and its prompt-fatigue half rested on proximity to the 2026-08-12/13 re-prompts, which this feature's merge will not have. Published together with the wording itself in lib/legal/copy.ts (feature 014).

camera_inference.rationale: Initial publication of the camera-and-inference consent. The first revision of a text is material by definition — there is no earlier wording anyone could already hold, so every user must be asked before a calibration or a monitoring session captures anything. Published together with the wording itself in lib/consent/copy.ts (feature 013, P4).

Terminology (#198), the camera-gate half of the same change. The lede now names both words for the same surface — "A monitoring session is what the rest of the app calls a check-in" — and the declining-scope list renames the questionnaire to the weekly work-environment survey. Judged MATERIAL for the same reason as terms_privacy@2026-08-12.1, and more sharply here: this gate is the last text a person reads before the camera turns on, and the sentence that tells them what declining costs them is one of the sentences that changed. Nothing the gate permits or blocks has changed. Published together with the wording itself in lib/consent/copy.ts.
